PKTWALK.t: The Node app writes the query to its database socket. The kernel builds an IP packet. The destination is not inside the VM's /32, so the route table says: send it to the gateway.
The OS wraps the packet in an Ethernet frame for the gateway. It got the gateway's MAC from an ARP reply that the data plane made up. Nothing was broadcast.

The data plane takes the frame from the vNIC and drops the MAC header: it routes on IP only. It checks the egress rules for kade-api-1, records the connection, and looks up where 10.10.2.5 lives. The answer was pushed to it long before this packet.
f: recorded, so the reply can come back

PKTWALK.t: The packet is wrapped in Google's own outer envelope, addressed from host A to host B, and sent across Google's physical network. Your packet is inside, unchanged. Neither VM ever sees the outer envelope.
f: host A → host B (Google's addresses, hidden from you)

PKTWALK.t: Host B unwraps the packet and checks the ingress rules for kade-db. kade-allow-internal allows everything from 10.10.0.0/16, so it passes. This is finding 4 from chapter 0: any VM in kade-vpc would pass here, on any port.

The data plane hands kade-db a normal-looking frame, as if it came from its own gateway. kade-db sees the real source IP and port. Its reply goes back the same way, and host A lets it in because the connection was recorded in step 3.
f: allowed by the recorded connection, no rule needed

SCOPE: One object for the whole planet. Subnets in any region belong to it.
Rules belong to the VPC, so they are global. Every host's data plane loads the ones it needs.
Routes belong to the VPC network, so they are global too.
One region, stretched over all its zones.
It runs on one physical host in one zone.
It lives in the same zone as the VM that uses it.
Cloud Router and the Cloud NAT on it are set up per region.
A global external IP, announced from Google's edge all over the world.
Regional external IPs are used by VMs, Cloud NAT and regional load balancers.
Deployed to one region; Google runs it across that region's zones.
Set up per region, with two interfaces for redundancy.

ss: Ephemeral internal addresses stay with the VM across stop and start. This is why kade-db has kept 10.10.2.5 so far.
del: The address goes back to the subnet and the next new VM may get it.
rec: The new VM gets the next free address in the subnet. Anything hardcoded to the old one breaks.
rm: A network card always has a primary internal address. You can change it only by recreating the card or the VM.

ss: Nothing changes; the reservation stays attached.
del: The reservation stays in the project with status RESERVED, ready for the next VM. Internal reservations are free.
rec: Same address, if you ask for it.
Create the new VM with --private-network-ip set to the reserved address or its name.
rm: It goes back to RESERVED and can be given to another VM.

ss: The address is released when the VM stops, and a new one is picked when it starts. This is the outage at the top of this chapter.
del: There is no way to get the same address back.
rec: A rebuilt VM gets a fresh address from Google's pool.
rm: Removing the access config releases the address immediately.

ss: The address stays attached, and still counts as in use while the VM is stopped.
del: Kept, and now billed as idle.
The reservation returns to RESERVED. Reattach it or release it; an idle static address costs more than one in use.
rec: Same address, if you ask for it.
Attach the reserved address to the new VM with --address.
rm: Kept, and now billed as idle.
It returns to RESERVED. Give it to something or release it.

QUERYBOOK: Which requests failed in the last hour?

resource.type="http_load_balancer"
httpRequest.status>=500
Every 5xx at the front door.
Group mentally by jsonPayload.statusDetails: backend errors, timeouts, or no backend.
Who produced the errors? (Log Analytics SQL)

SELECT JSON_VALUE(json_payload.statusDetails) AS who, COUNT(*) AS n
FROM `kade-prod.global._Default._AllLogs`
WHERE resource.type = "http_load_balancer"
  AND http_request.status >= 500
  AND timestamp > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR)
GROUP BY who ORDER BY n DESC
A count of errors by who produced them.
Mostly response_sent_by_backend: an app problem. failed_to_pick_backend or backend_timeout: a platform problem.
Follow one request everywhere (by CF-Ray)

jsonPayload.cf_ray="8c1a2b3c4d5e6f70-CMB"
OR httpRequest.requestUrl:"8c1a2b3c4d5e6f70"
Every app line kade-api printed for that request.
Then take the trace ID from one of them to find the load balancer and Cloud Run entries.
Which Cloud Armor rule blocked this?

resource.type="http_load_balancer"
jsonPayload.enforcedSecurityPolicy.outcome="DENY"
Every request Cloud Armor refused.
enforcedSecurityPolicy.priority names the rule; preconfiguredExprIds names the exact WAF signature, for tuning false positives.
Which requests were slow?

resource.type="http_load_balancer"
httpRequest.latency>"2s"
Requests that took more than 2 seconds end to end.
Check if they share a URL (one slow endpoint) or a time (the database or PayGate was slow then).
Is the firewall blocking something to kade-worker?

logName:"compute.googleapis.com%2Ffirewall"
jsonPayload.disposition="DENIED"
jsonPayload.connection.dest_ip="10.10.1.20"
Denied connections to kade-worker, with the rule that denied them.
Needs logging on the rule; implied denies only show if the deny-all-log rule exists.
Are PayGate calls dropped at NAT?

resource.type="nat_gateway"
jsonPayload.allocation_status="DROPPED"
Connections Cloud NAT could not translate.
OUT_OF_RESOURCES: ports ran out (chapter 7, section 05).
Who talks to PayGate? (flow logs)

logName:"vpc_flows"
jsonPayload.connection.dest_ip="192.0.2.10"
Sampled connections to PayGate, with source instance or Cloud Run service.
Unexpected sources mean something else is calling the payment API.
Who changed a firewall rule?

logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"
protoPayload.methodName:"compute.firewalls"
Every create, update and delete of firewall rules, with who did it.
Admin Activity audit logs are always on and free.

Site down for everyone: Uptime check results by region; Cloudflare status page
All regions failing: likely the whole front door. One region: a local internet problem, usually not yours.
If all regions fail, go to step 2.
A 52x page means Cloudflare is up but the origin leg failed. Read the code with chapter 13's error decoder.
No 52x but nothing loads: check DNS (dig +short api.kade.lk) and Cloudflare. A 52x: step 3.
What does the load balancer say?
failed_to_pick_backend: no backend. denied_by_security_policy: Cloud Armor. Nothing logged at all: requests are not reaching the LB (origin lock, certificate, forwarding rule).
The latest revision not ready, or failing to start, means a bad deploy.
Roll back: gcloud run services update-traffic kade-api --to-revisions=LAST_GOOD_REVISION_NAME=100
Many 502 / 503 errors: The "Who produced the errors?" query (16.1 cookbook)
response_sent_by_backend: the app returned them. failed_to_pick_backend or backend_timeout: the platform.
Cloud Run app logs, severity>=ERROR, around the same minutes
An exception, or a dependency (database, PayGate) refusing or timing out.
Is Cloud Run at its limit?
Dashboard: instance count against max instances
Pinned at max: requests queue and some get 503.
Raise max instances or find what made requests slow.
Is the database or PayGate the cause?
Dashboard: Cloud SQL connections and NAT drops
Connections at max: pool settings or a leak. NAT drops: ports (chapter 7).
Fix the dependency; the 5xx follow it down.
Slow for everyone: Is it slow at the LB, or inside the app?
Dashboard: total latency vs backend latency
Both high: the app is slow. Total high but backend normal: the problem is before the backend (Cloudflare, TLS, network).
"Which requests were slow?" query, grouped by URL
One endpoint: a slow query or call. All endpoints: something shared.
Cloud SQL query insights; app logs with timings around PayGate calls
A slow query, or a dependency taking seconds.
Payments failing: Is it all payments or some?
App logs for PayGate calls: errors by message
"Connection refused" or "403" from PayGate: the allow-list. Timeouts: the network or PayGate.
NAT drops query (16.1 cookbook); dashboard NAT panel
OUT_OF_RESOURCES during busy minutes: ports per VM too low (chapter 7).
Raise min ports or turn on dynamic port allocation; reuse connections.
Is traffic leaving from the right IP?
From kade-worker: curl -s ifconfig.me  ·  Connectivity Test Cloud Run → PayGate
Anything other than 34.87.200.7 means a path skips NAT (an external IP, or Cloud Run egress not set to all-traffic).
Fix the path; PayGate only accepts 34.87.200.7.
One feature returns 403: Load balancer logs for that URL: statusDetails
denied_by_security_policy: Cloud Armor. response_sent_by_backend: the app's own permission check.
"Which Cloud Armor rule blocked this?" query
A preconfigured WAF signature on a legitimate request is a false positive.
Exclude that signature for that path, or put the rule in preview while tuning.
VMs keep being recreated: Is the group stuck below its size?
gcloud compute instance-groups managed list-instances kade-media-mig --region=asia-southeast1
VMs cycling through CREATING, RECREATING again and again: autohealing is replacing them.
Logs: protoPayload.methodName="compute.instances.repair.recreateInstance", then a new VM's serial output
Recreated within minutes of starting: the initial delay is shorter than startup (a boot loop). Recreated after running a while: the app really breaks.
Boot loop: step 3. App breaks: the app logs (Ops Agent).
Can the health check reach the app?
Connectivity Test from 35.191.0.1 to a VM on 8080; curl localhost:8080/healthz on the VM over IAP
Firewall step DROPPED: the rule for Google's ranges targets the wrong service account. Local curl fails: the app does not start.
Raise the initial delay, fix the rule, or roll back to the previous template (chapter 12.2, command 9).
Office cannot reach GCP: Are the tunnels and BGP up?
gcloud compute vpn-tunnels list; gcloud compute routers get-status kade-vpn-router
Tunnel not ESTABLISHED or BGP down: the VPN itself.
Connectivity Test from the office IP to the destination
DROPPED at a firewall step: a missing rule. At a route step: an advertisement missing (chapter 15).
ping -M do -s 1432 from kade-worker to the office
Small pings work, big ones fail: MTU (chapter 15 section 06).
Clamp MSS on the office router.

CONNTEST.take: Every check passes, and the test names the exact route it used. Saved, it becomes a one-click check after any change to routes, peering or firewall.

steps: no allow rule matches; implied deny ingress (65535)
CONNTEST.take: The test stops at the exact step and names the cause: the implied deny. Without logging or a real packet, you know which rule to add (chapter 15's kade-warehouse-to-inventory).

steps: Cloud Run kade-api, Direct VPC egress from sn-run
CONNTEST.take: For internet destinations the test can only follow the path to the edge of Google's network. It confirms the route and the NAT IP; whether PayGate answers is up to PayGate.

VMs and IPs: VMs with external IPs, except those listed
VMs that can forward packets (routers, NAT VMs)
Serial console access. Note: this also removes the break-glass path from chapter 6.1

Peering with networks not on the list. Private services access (chapter 9) also uses peering: test in dry run before enforcing
Using a Shared VPC host that is not approved

Authorized networks lists on Cloud SQL

Give a VM an external IP: would be allowed for a Network Admin
Open SSH to 0.0.0.0/0 with a VPC rule: no org constraint for rule contents
the folder policy denies 22 from the internet before VPC rules are checked (chapter 5.2)
Security Admin may create the rule
the rule exists but does nothing; the change alert fires, SCC reports OPEN_SSH_PORT

req.what: The phone asks DNS for www.kade.lk. Cloudflare is authoritative, and the record is orange, so the answer is a Cloudflare address, not Kadé's load balancer.
req.dec: Cloudflare holds the zone; proxied (orange) record
req.pkt:
UDP 53 (or DNS over HTTPS)
Q: www.kade.lk A?
A: 104.21.48.12   (Cloudflare)

req.what: The phone opens TLS to Cloudflare's Colombo edge, which presents its Universal SSL certificate. Cloudflare checks its WAF and bot rules, assigns a CF-Ray ID, and looks in its cache: this size has never been asked for, so it is a miss.
req.dec: Edge certificate; Always Use HTTPS; minimum TLS 1.2; Cache Rules

req.what: Cloudflare opens its own connection to 34.120.88.10, checks Google's certificate (Full strict), and adds CF-Connecting-IP and the secret x-kade-edge header. Google's front end ends TLS at the target proxy. Cloud Armor checks: a Cloudflare address, the right header, no WAF match. Allowed.
req.dec: SSL/TLS mode Full (strict); kade-https-proxy cert map and kade-tls; kade-edge-policy origin lock

req.what: With the request decrypted, the URL map reads host www.kade.lk → path matcher web → longest path /media/* → kade-media-backend. Cloud CDN on that backend service also misses.
req.dec: kade-url-map host rule and path rule
req.pkt:
Host: www.kade.lk
Path: /media/rice-640w.jpg
→ backend service kade-media-backend

req.t: To a healthy VM, through the firewall
req.what: The backend service picks a healthy VM with spare capacity (RATE 80 per VM) and opens a new connection from Google's front end to port 8080 on its named port. The VM has no external IP; the packet arrives on its internal IP. kade-vpc's firewall checks: source 35.191.0.0/16, target service account sa-kade-media, tcp:8080. Allowed by kade-lb-to-media.
req.dec: Health check kade-media-hc; balancing mode; firewall rule by service account
req.log: Firewall rule log (kade-lb-to-media ALLOWED); VPC Flow Logs on sn-app

req.what: kade-media connects to db.kade.internal. The VM asks the metadata server at 169.254.169.254, which walks the resolution order: the private zone kade-internal matches and answers 10.10.32.3.
req.dec: Private zone kade-internal, visible to kade-vpc
req.log: Cloud DNS query logs (if the server policy logs)

req.what: The VM connects to 10.10.32.3:5432. The route for 10.10.32.0/20 comes from the private services access peering. Egress is allowed by the implied rule; Cloud SQL lives in Google's network, so no ingress rule is needed on Kadé's side. The connection is TLS, because the instance accepts encrypted connections only.
req.dec: PSA peering route; implied allow egress; Cloud SQL ENCRYPTED_ONLY
req.pkt:
10.10.1.31:40112 → 10.10.32.3:5432
TLS · SELECT … FROM photos WHERE sku='rice'
req.log: VPC Flow Logs (sn-app); Cloud SQL PostgreSQL log

req.what: The VM calls storage.googleapis.com, which resolves to a public Google address. With no external IP, the VM uses Private Google Access on sn-app: the default route sends it to Google, which accepts it and keeps it on Google's network. The VM's service account has read access to the bucket; no key file.
req.dec: PGA on sn-app (also enabled by Cloud NAT); default route; IAM on the bucket
req.log: Cloud Storage Data Access audit logs (if enabled); VPC Flow Logs

ret.what: Cloud Storage sends the bytes back. They match the connection the VM opened, so no rule is needed to let them in: the firewall is stateful.
Photo details come back over the same TLS connection. The VM resizes the image and adds a watermark.
ret.log: App log line (with CF-Ray and trace ID)

ret.what: The VM replies on the connection Google's front end opened. No egress rule is consulted for a reply. The response carries Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, so both caches may keep it.
ret.dec: Stateful firewall; the app's Cache-Control header
ret.log: Ops Agent: the VM's own access log

ret.what: Cloud CDN on kade-media-backend stores the image. The load balancer writes one log line: status 200, latency, statusDetails: response_sent_by_backend.
ret.dec: enableCDN on the backend service; CACHE_ALL_STATIC

ret.what: The response goes back to Cloudflare over TLS 2. Cloudflare's Cache Rule allows /media/*, so it keeps a copy too.
Cloudflare answers over TLS 1. Headers show server: cloudflare and cf-cache-status: MISS. The next shopper in Colombo gets HIT, answered in milliseconds without touching Google at all.
ret.log: Uptime check would see the same path (ch 16.2)

breaks.label: www set to grey (DNS only)
breaks.what: DNS now returns 34.120.88.10 directly, so the shopper connects to Google without Cloudflare. No x-kade-edge header, and the source is not a Cloudflare address.
breaks.log: LB log: statusDetails denied_by_security_policy · enforcedSecurityPolicy.priority 2147483647 (default deny)
breaks.fix: Set the record back to orange. Every record pointing at the load balancer must be proxied.

breaks.label: SSL/TLS mode Flexible
breaks.what: Cloudflare talks plain HTTP to port 80. Kadé's HTTP forwarding rule answers with a 301 to https://, Cloudflare passes it on, the browser retries… forever.
breaks.log: LB log: many 301s on kade-http-rule for the same URL

breaks.label: New Cloudflare range not in the allow-list
breaks.what: Cloudflare starts using a new edge range. Requests from it fail the origin lock; requests from other edges still work.
breaks.log: LB log: denied_by_security_policy with remoteIp in an unlisted Cloudflare range
breaks.fix: Update the Cloudflare ranges in kade-edge-policy (or use the named list with Cloud Armor Enterprise).

breaks.label: Health-check firewall rule deleted
breaks.what: A clean-up removed kade-lb-to-media. Health checks from 35.191.0.0/16 are dropped, every VM is marked unhealthy, and autohealing starts recreating VMs that were fine.
breaks.log: LB log: statusDetails failed_to_pick_backend · system event compute.instances.repair.recreateInstance
breaks.fix: Recreate the rule: tcp:8080 from Google's ranges to sa-kade-media.

breaks.label: Autohealing initial delay 0
breaks.what: During a sale the group scales out. New VMs are judged before the app has started and are recreated in a loop, so the group never reaches its size.
breaks.log: instance_group/size below target · repeated recreateInstance events
breaks.fix: Set the initial delay above the slowest startup (180 s).

breaks.label: Private zone not visible to kade-vpc
breaks.what: The private zone kade-internal lost its kade-vpc authorization. db.kade.internal falls through to public DNS, which has no such name.
breaks.log: App log: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND db.kade.internal · DNS query log NXDOMAIN
breaks.fix: Authorize kade-vpc on the zone again.

breaks.label: sn-app loses Private Google Access
breaks.what: sn-app was removed from Cloud NAT (which had turned PGA on) and nobody turned PGA on by hand. The VM has no external IP, so Cloud Storage is unreachable.
breaks.sees: 504 after a long wait on new photo sizes; cached sizes still work
breaks.log: App log: timeout to storage.googleapis.com · flow logs: SYNs with no reply
breaks.fix: Turn on Private Google Access on sn-app.

req.what: DNS and the edge leg work as in chapter 18.1. Differences: a Cache Rule bypasses cache for api.kade.lk, and Cloudflare's own rate limit on checkout runs here, keyed on the real shopper.
req.dec: Orange record; Cache Rule bypass for the API; Cloudflare rate limiting

req.what: Full (strict) TLS to 34.120.88.10; the origin lock passes (Cloudflare address + secret header). The login rate-limit rule does not match this path, and the WAF rules find nothing.
req.dec: kade-edge-policy: origin lock, WAF, rate limit keyed on CF-Connecting-IP

req.t: To Cloud Run, through the serverless NEG
req.what: The URL map sends api.kade.lk to kade-api-backend, whose backend is a serverless NEG. There is no health check and no firewall rule: Cloud Run is not in kade-vpc. Instead, Cloud Run's ingress setting checks that the request came through a load balancer. It did.
req.dec: kade-url-map; serverless NEG kade-api-neg; ingress internal-and-cloud-load-balancing
req.pkt:
Google front end → Cloud Run (inside Google, not in the VPC)
X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.99, 104.23.211.40, 34.120.88.10
req.log: LB log; Cloud Run request log (not in VPC Flow Logs)

req.t: kade-api runs, and starts calling out
req.what: An instance of kade-api handles the request and logs a JSON line with the CF-Ray and trace ID. Every call it makes now leaves through Direct VPC egress into sn-run, because egress is all-traffic: it gets an address like 10.10.3.17 and follows kade-vpc's routes and firewall.
req.dec: Direct VPC egress into sn-run, all-traffic
req.log: Cloud Run app log (JSON, cf_ray, trace)

req.what: db.kade.internal is answered by the private zone (10.10.32.3). api.paygate.lk matches no private zone and is looked up on the internet (192.0.2.10).
req.dec: Resolution order: private zone, then public DNS

req.what: Over the private services access peering to Cloud SQL, encrypted. The order is saved as "pending payment" before PayGate is called, so a crash later cannot lose it.
req.dec: PSA peering route; ENCRYPTED_ONLY; connector or Auth Proxy
req.log: VPC Flow Logs on sn-run; Cloud SQL log

req.what: 192.0.2.10 matches only the default route, next hop the internet gateway. Cloud NAT covers sn-run, so the source is rewritten to 34.87.200.7 and one of the instance's reserved ports. The NAT keeps a record so the reply can come back.
req.dec: Default route; kade-nat covers sn-run; port allocation
req.log: NAT logs only on errors; VPC Flow Logs show the inside address

req.what: PayGate sees the request from 34.87.200.7, which is on its allow-list, and charges the card.
req.dec: Fixed NAT IP, given to PayGate before go-live
req.log: PayGate's own logs; kade-api app log with PayGate's reference

ret.what: PayGate answers 34.87.200.7:41877. Cloud NAT finds the record and rewrites the destination back to 10.10.3.17:51220. A packet from the internet with no matching record would be dropped.
The reply reaches the Cloud Run instance that made the call. No firewall rule is needed for replies.
kade-api updates the order from "pending payment" to "paid" over the open database connection.
kade-api answers. Cloud Run writes its request log with latency; the response carries Cache-Control: no-store.
ret.dec: App response; no caching for the API
ret.log: Cloud Run request log; LB log statusDetails response_sent_by_backend

ret.what: The load balancer returns the response to Cloudflare. Nothing is cached, by the bypass rule and the header.
Headers show cf-cache-status: DYNAMIC. The whole trip, two TLS legs, a database write, a payment provider and back, took about 900 ms, mostly PayGate.
ret.log: p95 latency panel on the dashboard (ch 16.2)

breaks.label: Rate limit keyed on IP, not CF-Connecting-IP
breaks.what: Cloud Armor counts requests per source IP, which is a handful of Cloudflare edges. One busy edge hits the limit and blocks everyone behind it.
breaks.sees: 429 Too Many Requests for many shoppers at once
breaks.log: LB log: enforcedSecurityPolicy outcome DENY, priority 100, the same few remoteIp values
breaks.fix: Key the rule on the CF-Connecting-IP header.

breaks.label: Cloud Run ingress set to internal
breaks.what: "internal" accepts traffic from the VPC only, not from the load balancer. Every request from the front end is refused.
breaks.log: LB log: 404 with response_sent_by_backend; no Cloud Run app log for those requests

breaks.label: Cloud Run at max instances
breaks.what: A sale pushes traffic past what max instances can serve. Requests queue, then are refused.
breaks.log: container/instance_count flat at max · Cloud Run request log 429
breaks.fix: Raise max instances, and check NAT ports and database connections can take the larger size.

breaks.label: App connects to Cloud SQL without TLS
breaks.what: A new release changed the database driver settings. Cloud SQL accepts encrypted connections only, so it refuses.
breaks.log: App log: "SSL is required" · Cloud SQL log: connection rejected
breaks.fix: Use the Cloud SQL connector or turn TLS back on in the driver.

breaks.label: sn-run removed from Cloud NAT
breaks.what: Traffic to PayGate enters sn-run and matches the default route, but no NAT covers the subnet and the instance has no external IP. Nothing leaves.
breaks.sees: Checkout spins, then fails after the timeout
breaks.log: App log: timeout to api.paygate.lk · flow logs: SYN with no reply · no NAT log at all

breaks.label: NAT ports run out during a sale
breaks.what: Each instance holds its reserved ports. Many short connections to the same PayGate IP and port use them all up; new ones are dropped.
breaks.sees: Some payments fail at peak, others work
breaks.fix: Reuse connections in the app; raise min ports or turn on dynamic port allocation.

breaks.label: Cloud Run egress private-ranges-only
breaks.what: Only private addresses go through the VPC. The call to PayGate skips Cloud NAT and leaves from a random Google address, which PayGate does not know.
breaks.log: App log: 403 from PayGate · no flow log entries to 192.0.2.10

QUIZ1.q: Google's front end sees the client as 104.23.211.40. What is that address?
QUIZ1.why: With an orange record, Cloudflare opens its own connection to the origin. The shopper's address travels in CF-Connecting-IP.

QUIZ1.q: Every photo request fails with 502 and the LB log says failed_to_pick_backend. What do you check first?
o: The health check and its firewall rule
QUIZ1.why: No healthy backend means health checks are failing. The most common cause is the firewall rule for 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22.

QUIZ1.q: Why does kade-media need no firewall rule to receive Cloud SQL's replies?
o: Cloud SQL is in the same subnet
The firewall is stateful: replies to an allowed connection pass
QUIZ1.why: A connection the VM opened is tracked, and its replies are let in automatically. There is no implied allow ingress.

QUIZ1.q: kade-media has no external IP. How does it read from Cloud Storage?
o: Through Private Google Access on sn-app
QUIZ1.why: Private Google Access lets VMs without external IPs reach Google APIs over Google's network. Cloud NAT turns it on, but Google API traffic does not use NAT ports.

QUIZ1.q: A visitor gets ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS. Which setting do you check?
QUIZ1.why: Flexible mode sends HTTP to the origin, which redirects to HTTPS, which Cloudflare fetches over HTTP again. Use Full (strict).

QUIZ1.q: Which log shows that the load balancer, not the app, produced an error?
QUIZ1.why: statusDetails says who answered: response_sent_by_backend means the app; failed_to_pick_backend or denied_by_security_policy mean the platform.

QUIZ2.q: PayGate rejects Kadé's calls after a deploy. The Cloud Run service shows egress private-ranges-only. Why does that matter?
o: Internet traffic skips Cloud NAT and leaves from a random Google IP
The load balancer cannot reach Cloud Run
QUIZ2.why: Only all-traffic sends internet-bound calls through the VPC and Cloud NAT, which gives the fixed 34.87.200.7.

QUIZ2.q: Why do VPC Flow Logs never show the shopper's request reaching kade-api?
o: Flow logs are off by default
The LB to Cloud Run hop does not pass through kade-vpc
QUIZ2.why: Cloud Run is outside the VPC; only its outgoing calls through Direct VPC egress enter sn-run. Use LB and Cloud Run logs for shopper traffic.

QUIZ2.q: Some payments fail only at peak, and the NAT log shows OUT_OF_RESOURCES. What is the first fix to try?
o: Reuse connections to PayGate in the app
QUIZ2.why: Each connection to the same destination needs its own NAT port. Reusing connections cuts the number needed; then consider dynamic port allocation.

QUIZ2.q: What lets Cloud Run accept requests from the load balancer but not from its run.app address?
QUIZ2.why: Cloud Run is not in the VPC, so firewall rules do not apply. Its ingress setting is the gate.

QUIZ2.q: Which control stops a developer re-adding an external IP to a VM next month?
QUIZ2.why: Org policies refuse the change itself, for everyone, in every project under the folder.

QUIZ2.q: Cloud Armor rate-limits by source IP and many shoppers get 429. Why?
o: All requests come from a few Cloudflare edge IPs
QUIZ2.why: Behind Cloudflare, the source IP is Cloudflare's. Key the rate limit on the CF-Connecting-IP header.
